# Contract: Landing Page

*Generated by spec-writer. Hand edits are overwritten on regeneration.*

## Prerequisites

These conditions describe the environment in which items in this
contract are exercised. Producing them is part of the feature's
deliverable, alongside the implementation itself — a contract whose
prerequisites are not yet satisfied is not failing, it is still being
built. Once the feature is delivered, any missing condition halts item
execution until it is restored.

**Runtime services:**
- the `apps/web` Next.js application is running (dev server or production build) and reachable by a browser
- a browser (or browser-automation engine) is available to drive UI items

**Configuration:**
- the frontend recognizes a cookie named `videomax_session` (any non-empty value) as an "authenticated visitor" signal for the `/` route. This cookie can be set directly (via browser automation or an HTTP client) to simulate an authenticated visitor without depending on any other feature's login flow — the mechanism is entirely delivered by this feature. Used by: UI-REDIRECT-01.

## Quality gates

Each gate must pass for the feature to be considered ready.

- **Lint** — `npm run lint --workspace apps/web` — ESLint reports no errors across the frontend app.
- **Typecheck** — `npm run typecheck --workspace apps/web` — TypeScript compiles with no type errors (`tsc --noEmit`).
- **Unit/component tests** — `npm run test --workspace apps/web` — the Vitest + React Testing Library suite passes.
- **End-to-end tests** — `npm run test:e2e --workspace apps/web` — the Playwright suite passes against a running build.
- **Build** — `npm run build --workspace apps/web` — the Next.js production build completes without errors.

## Coverage Manifest

| PRD Acceptance Criterion | Covered by |
|---|---|
| Page loads at `/` without requiring authentication | UI-LANDING-01 |
| Primary "Create account" CTA links to `/register` | UI-CTA-01 |
| Top-right "Log in" link routes to `/login` | UI-NAV-01 |
| Authenticated users who visit `/` are redirected to `/app` | UI-REDIRECT-01 |
| Visual design follows a minimalist, HubSpot-inspired style (generous white space, flat layout, restrained accent color) | UI-VISUAL-01 |

## UI

**Verification mode:** Render the surface, drive it with user-like inputs (clicks, typing, gestures); assert observable surface state (DOM, accessibility tree, visible text, navigation).

### Public Landing Page

**Common given:** no `videomax_session` cookie is present (anonymous visitor).

#### `UI-LANDING-01` — page loads at / without authentication
- given: (default)
- when: navigate to `/`
- then:
  - the landing content renders directly (no login wall, no redirect)
  - the hero section is visible with the product name and a one-sentence value proposition
  - the "how it works" strip is visible showing Upload → Transcribe → Summarize, in that order
  - a footer is visible at the bottom of the page

### Primary Call-to-Action

**Common given:** anonymous visitor on `/`.

#### `UI-CTA-01` — Create account CTA routes to /register
- given: (default)
- when: click the "Create account" button in the hero section
- then:
  - the browser navigates to `/register`

### Navigation

**Common given:** anonymous visitor on `/`.

#### `UI-NAV-01` — Log in link routes to /login
- given: (default)
- when: click the "Log in" link in the top-right of the navigation bar
- then:
  - the browser navigates to `/login`

### Authenticated Redirect

#### `UI-REDIRECT-01` — authenticated visitor is redirected away from /
- given: the `videomax_session` cookie is present with a non-empty value (simulating an authenticated visitor)
- when: navigate to `/`
- then:
  - the browser ends up on `/app`
  - the landing content (hero, how-it-works, footer) is never rendered

### Visual Identity

#### `UI-VISUAL-01` — minimalist, HubSpot-inspired visual style
- given: anonymous visitor on `/`
- when: view the rendered page
- then:
  - the layout shows generous white space throughout
  - the design is flat, with no heavy imagery or gradients
  - typography follows a clear hierarchy (distinct sizes/weights for headline, subhead, body)
  - a single restrained accent color is used consistently across CTA elements
- notes: subjective; manual review only
